_source: Svennberg E, Han JK, Caiani EG, et al. State of the Art of Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Electrophysiology in 2025: A Scientific Statement of the European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA) of the ESC, the Heart Rhythm Society (HRS), and the ESC Working Group on E-Cardiology. Europace 2025;27(5):euaf071. Items transcribed from the published checklist table.
_note: The checklist carries 29 numbered items plus two lettered items, i) Title and ii) Conclusion.

items.name: Title
items.text: Include clear terms to identify the study as using artificial intelligence, machine learning or other specific terms

items.name: Intended clinical use
items.text: Clearly describe the intended use and where in clinical workflow the model can be used and the objective

items.name: Clinical benefit
items.text: Added benefit of AI compared with standard clinical care (gold standard)

items.name: Data collection
items.text: Describe how data was collected

items.name: Source (of data)
items.text: Describe the study design or source of input data and how it was acquired

items.name: Development data set (model training data set)
items.text: Describe the data set

items.name: Participants
items.text: Describe the participants in the data sets, including eligibility criteria (inclusion and exclusion criteria)

items.name: Comparator
items.text: Provide clear definition of how the gold standard was collected. Clearly describe the gold standard and ground truth

items.name: Testing data set
items.text: Describe the testing data set, in particular defining the data set split

items.name: Sample size
items.text: Explain how the study size was arrived at

items.name: Outcome
items.text: Clearly define standardized and reproducible outcome of clinical relevance

items.name: Data type (source)
items.text: Clearly describe the data type for the study, including pre-processing

items.name: Data preparation
items.text: Input data handling, data augmentation and selection prior to analysis by the AI system

items.name: Balanced groups
items.text: Clearly state how/if groups were balanced

items.name: Data issues (missingness / poor data / duplication / outliers)
items.text: Describe how handling of data of poor quality/noise/missing data was performed

items.name: Feature engineering (extraction / selection / reduction)
items.text: If features are used, feature selection should be described including by whom features were extracted

items.name: Legal framework
items.text: Clearly state if the software has been approved by legal authorities, e.g. Certificate of conformity (EU) or FDA approval

items.name: Explainability
items.text: Is the AI model explainable on the patient level or on a global or local level

items.name: Ethical approval
items.text: Provide information on ethical approval of the study

items.name: Fairness
items.text: Describe inclusion of relevant groups in the dataset

items.name: Data availability/code sharing
items.text: Is the data available on a public website? Is the code available?

items.name: Trial registration
items.text: In case of a trial, clearly state if and where the trial is registered

items.name: Participants
items.text: Baseline demographics (internal and external validation data)

items.name: Training performance
items.text: Provide results from the training data set

items.name: Internal validation
items.text: The results from the testing data set

items.name: External validation
items.text: The results from the external validation data set

items.name: Model performance (internal and external validation)
items.text: Choose appropriate metric selection for reporting

items.name: Performance errors
items.text: Analysis of performance errors and how they were identified

items.name: Performance compared with classic statistical methods
items.text: What did the model add?

items.name: Generalizability
items.text: Discuss the level of generalizability of the results obtained

items.name: Conclusion
items.text: Is the conclusion supported by the dataset?
